intro: Picture this: you roll into Sa Kaeo in the evening, looking for somewhere quiet and clean with a parking spot right outside your room, no jostling for space, then wake up to coffee on the balcony looking out over a green garden before you carry on. Lemin Resort is a small resort of about 16 rooms in the Tha Kasem area of Mueang Sa Kaeo district · The resort is made up of single-storey loft-style bungalows in exposed concrete mixed with wood, set along a plot with a garden and lawn, and every room has a private balcony · It suits people driving through, coming on errands, or using Sa Kaeo as a stopover before crossing to Aranyaprathet, who want a budget place that is cleaner and quieter than a hotel in town · Prices start at around THB 520/night · The average score sits at about 8.4 (though the number of reviews on the booking platforms is still small, since this is a small property)

body.html: Who Lemin Resort suits — to put it as plainly as possible, Lemin Resort is for people looking for a "small, quiet, clean, budget resort" in Sa Kaeo province, rather than a big hotel with a fancy lobby, a pool, or every facility under one roof · The resort is made up of single-storey loft-style bungalows in exposed concrete mixed with wood — clean-looking and fairly new — set along a plot with a garden and lawn, which gives it a more private and open feel than a tower hotel in town · According to the booking platforms, it is rated at around 2 stars, has about 16 rooms, and sits in Tha Kasem subdistrict, Mueang Sa Kaeo district · The people it suits best are travellers driving their own car who want easy parking right by the room, people coming on errands or government business in Sa Kaeo town, families or couples who want a quiet atmosphere on a budget, and travellers using Sa Kaeo as a stopover before crossing to Aranyaprathet or the Thai-Cambodian border · On the other hand, if you expect full facilities like a swimming pool, gym, an in-resort restaurant open for every meal, or chain-hotel-level service, a small place like this may not be the answer, and you should look at a mid-sized hotel in town instead · One thing to say straight up: this is a small property, so the number of reviews on the platforms is still very small. The average score you see (around 8.4) comes from a small sample, so it should be read as a "trend" rather than a settled figure — but the trend is fairly positive, especially on cleanliness and quiet

Location and getting around — the interesting thing about Lemin Resort is its location in the Tha Kasem area, a subdistrict of Mueang Sa Kaeo district · The address is 6 Moo 2, Tha Kasem subdistrict, Mueang Sa Kaeo district · This kind of location has both upsides and points worth understanding before you book · The upside is that it sits outside the dense built-up area, so it is quiet, surrounded by trees and garden, and parking is easy because you are not competing with anyone — ideal for people driving their own car · At the same time it is only a short drive of a few minutes from Sa Kaeo town, so running errands, shopping, or finding a restaurant in town is no trouble · For those travelling further afield, Sa Kaeo sits on a major route to the Thai-Cambodian border. The permanent Aranyaprathet crossing (Rong Kluea Market) lies further out towards Aranyaprathet district, a fair drive away, and the province is also a starting point for nature trips such as Pang Sida National Park, known for its waterfalls and butterflies during the rainy season · The thing to note about getting around is that the Tha Kasem area is quiet and mostly residential, without dense shops or restaurants within walking distance, and hailing public or ride-hailing transport may not be as easy as in a big city — having your own car makes staying here the most convenient · For those not driving, we recommend asking the resort ahead about transport and nearby restaurants
"Nice and quiet, easy parking, friendly front-desk service, clean rooms with no musty smell, air-con nice and cold. Overall fine — good for a stopover on the road."

Room types and decor — Lemin Resort has about 16 rooms in total, built as single-storey loft-style bungalows finished in exposed concrete mixed with wood — clean-looking and contemporary, not a high-rise hotel block · From the information available, the rooms come mainly in two types, Standard and Superior, with the main difference being room size and detail: Standard is the most budget-friendly option, while Superior is a little larger · A point many people like is that every room has a private balcony for coffee or relaxing while looking out over the garden — the charm of a bungalow-style resort that a tower hotel in town can't offer · In-room facilities are complete for this price range, including air conditioning, cable TV, fridge, minibar, water heater, direct-dial phone, and a private bathroom with a shower · Real reviews agree that the rooms are clean, free of musty smells, and the air-con is nice and cold — which matters a lot for budget upcountry stays, since some places at a similar price have stuffy or poorly cleaned rooms · Because it is a small, fairly new resort, the rooms generally look tidy and well kept · One thing to understand is that, as a small 2-star property, the decor leans towards simple and clean rather than luxurious, and there may not be as many in-room extras as a big hotel — no coffee machine or premium bedding sets, for instance — which is reasonable for the price

Facilities and shared spaces — because it is a small resort, the facilities at Lemin Resort lean towards simplicity and easy-going stays rather than having everything like a big resort · The highlight many people mention is free private parking, a real advantage upcountry, since you can park conveniently right by your room or within the resort grounds without worrying about space or your car's security · There is also free Wi-Fi throughout, a terrace, a shared lounge, a 24-hour reception, and room service · The grounds have a garden and lawn that keep the atmosphere shady and quiet, good for sitting and relaxing or getting some morning air · To be honest, there is no swimming pool or gym, which is normal for a small resort at this price; if a pool is your main priority, this may not be the place · But for a stopover on the road, an errand trip, or a quiet rest, the facilities on offer are enough and worth the price · What wins people over at a small place like this is the cleanliness and close, attentive care rather than the number of facilities

Food and nearby restaurants — food at Lemin Resort is simple, in keeping with the size of the place · According to the platforms, it offers an Asian breakfast, and some room packages include breakfast in the price, which you should check carefully when booking, since at small properties some packages include it and some don't · As a small resort, it does not have a restaurant open for every meal like a big hotel; for lunch or dinner you will mostly need to head out to find somewhere in the Tha Kasem area or drive into Sa Kaeo town, which is not far · The upside of the location is that Sa Kaeo town has a variety of local eateries, à la carte spots, cafés, and markets to choose from, just a few minutes' drive away · For those driving their own car, the in-room fridge and minibar help a lot, since you can buy food and drinks to keep in the room · The tip is: if you arrive late or don't want to go out, bring some food in the car just in case, or ask the resort ahead about restaurants and food-ordering options · Overall, food is not the main strength here, but it isn't a big problem either, because the location is close to a town with plenty of options

Service — service at a small property like Lemin Resort is quite different from a chain hotel, and it's worth setting expectations right from the start · The upside is that small places often offer close, friendly care · The real reviews that exist (though few in number) agree that the front-desk staff are good and friendly, helpful with check-in and information · The platforms also state there is a 24-hour reception and room service, which is good for a place at this level, especially for those arriving late · That said, the limitation to accept is that a small property's service won't be as complete or formal as a big hotel — no concierge, no multiple departments, and at some times there may be limited staff on duty · On top of that, because reviews are still few, the picture of service isn't settled enough to draw a full conclusion · The tip is to communicate clearly with the resort before your stay — about check-in/check-out times, breakfast, and any special requests — to keep things smooth

Voices from real reviews (both praise and gripes) — to be upfront, Lemin Resort is a small property with very few reviews on the platforms, so the picture isn't as settled or comprehensive as a big hotel with hundreds or thousands of reviews · From what can be gathered, the average score is around 8.4/10 in the "very good" range, with sub-scores that stand out on value and staff service · On the praise side, what people mention consistently is the quiet atmosphere, clean rooms with no musty smell, nice cold air-con, easy parking, good and friendly front-desk service, and good value for the room condition · Many say it's very good for a stopover on the road or an errand trip, because it's easy to find and easy to come and go · On the points-to-note side, most aren't about room quality but about being a "small property" — a fairly quiet location away from shops within walking distance, suited to people with a car; no pool or big-resort facilities; and the small number of reviews, which limits the information available for a decision · The overall picture is a place that "stands out for cleanliness, quiet, and value, in exchange for simple facilities and a location suited to people with a car"

"Great value for the room — clean, cold air-con, parking right by the room is convenient. The only catch is you have to drive out to find restaurants in town; it's quiet around the property, but with a car it's no problem at all."

Price comparison and value — Lemin Resort's starting price is around THB 520/night for a Standard room and around THB 850/night for a Superior at regular rates (based on booking-platform data; actual prices may change with the season and promotions) · Compared with other places in Sa Kaeo province, the selling point here isn't luxury or full facilities but getting a clean bungalow room with a private balcony, in a quiet setting, with free parking, at a budget price · For a couple of hundred baht, getting a clean room with cold air-con and garden space around you is very good value for people driving through or coming on errands · Compared with budget chain hotels in town (such as the Hop Inn group) at a similar price, Lemin's advantage is the quiet resort atmosphere with a garden and balcony, while the trade-off is a location away from shops and a less complete set of services · In short, the value here depends on how much you value "quiet, clean rooms, and easy parking at a budget price" — if that's you, this price is very good value · But if you want to walk everywhere without a car, or you want a pool and full service, there may be a better fit elsewhere

What to know before booking — a few things help make a stay at Lemin Resort smoother · One, it suits people with a car most, because the Tha Kasem area is quiet and away from shops within walking distance — if you're not driving, ask the resort ahead about transport and nearby restaurants · Two, on breakfast and room packages, check clearly whether the rate you book includes breakfast, since packages at small properties can differ · Three, there is no pool or gym here, so set your facility expectations accordingly · Four, if you arrive late, give your check-in time in advance, because even with 24-hour service, a small property is one to coordinate with ahead for peace of mind · Five, since the number of reviews on the platforms is still small, we recommend looking at photos of the actual room you'll get and asking for details before confirming · Six, check-in is after 14:00 and check-out around 12:00 by standard, but confirm again with the resort · Seven, if you plan nature trips such as Pang Sida National Park or crossing to Aranyaprathet, allow travel time, as they're within a drive that needs planning

Verdict — from the information and real reviews gathered, Lemin Resort is the best fit for people who want a small, quiet resort with clean rooms, private balconies, and easy parking in Sa Kaeo province on a budget · Its charm is the garden-bungalow atmosphere, more relaxing than a tower hotel in town, clean rooms with cold air-con, and a location with easy parking that's still a few minutes from town — very good for a stopover, an errand trip, or as a base before nature and border trips · But it has to be said honestly that this is a small property with no pool or big-resort facilities, a quiet location suited to people with a car, and still few reviews on the platforms, so read the score as a trend · If you're looking for somewhere you can walk everywhere without a car, or you want a pool and full service like a big hotel, this may not be the answer, and a mid-sized hotel in Sa Kaeo town may suit better · But for people who understand what a small resort is, and who value cleanliness, quiet, and value — Lemin Resort gives you "a clean bungalow room in a quiet garden at a lovely price" that's not easy to find in the Tha Kasem area of Sa Kaeo
